# The numeric families are the trap: `Integer`'s lattice parent is

# to 0. `eq`/`deq` require concrete operands; use `teq` to compare types.

column1: # ── deq compares typed containers by VALUE, not render (NUR033) ───────

# same way it already ignores flexness. Before this rule deq fell back
# to the rendered form (`[:Integer]` vs `[1 2]`), which was a third
# equality notion and broke transitivity with cross-leaf pairs.

…and to an identically-typed twin

column1: # ── Function values: eq is identity, deq is content (NUR031) ─────────
# green on the interpreter and compile-FAILED on a pre-existing rule
# with nothing to do with equality: any fn value reaching a non-inert
# word was declined outright. eq / neq / deq / canon only ever READ a fn
# value — identity is a token minted once per authored function and
# copied by value, content is canon — so they now declare CompileReadsFn
# and the value rides as an ordinary const operand.
def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] f/v eq f/v
